CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFPROCPARAM

Each CFPROCPARAM inside a CFSTOREDPROC supplies one parameter, in the order the procedure declares them. Input parameters carry a value; output parameters name a CFML variable that receives the result.

Category

Database manipulation

Syntax

<CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In/Out/InOut"
    VARIABLE="variable_name"
    DBVARNAME="db_variable_name"
    VALUE="parameter_value"
    CFSQLTYPE="parameter_datatype"
    MAXLENGTH="length"
    SCALE="decimal_places"
    NULL="Yes/No">

Attributes

TYPE
Optional, default "In". In passes a value, Out receives one, InOut does both.
VARIABLE
Required for Out and InOut. CFML variable that receives the output value.
DBVARNAME
Optional. Name of the parameter in the procedure, such as @dept, for drivers that bind by name.
VALUE
Required for In and InOut. The value to pass.
CFSQLTYPE
Required. One of the CF_SQL_ types listed under CFQUERYPARAM.
MAXLENGTH
Optional. Maximum length of the value.
SCALE
Optional. Decimal places of a numeric value.
NULL
Optional, default "No". Yes passes SQL NULL.

Usage

Because KoldFusion's flat-file driver cannot run stored procedures, CFPROCPARAM is parsed but does nothing on its own; the enclosing CFSTOREDPROC throws a Database exception before any parameter is used, so an Out variable is never set. Give such variables a default with CFPARAM, as the example does.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFPARAM NAME="HeadCount" DEFAULT="(not returned)">
<CFTRY>
  <CFSTOREDPROC PROCEDURE="sp_CountStaff" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
    <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_VARCHAR" DBVARNAME="@dept" VALUE="Engineering">
    <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="Out" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_INTEGER" DBVARNAME="@total" VARIABLE="HeadCount">
  </CFSTOREDPROC>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Database">
    <CFOUTPUT><P>Caught a #CFCATCH.Type# exception: #CFCATCH.Message#</P></CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
<CFQUERY NAME="Counted" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT COUNT(*) AS Total FROM Employees WHERE Department = 'Engineering'
</CFQUERY>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TD>Out parameter HeadCount</TD><TD>#HeadCount#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Same answer from CFQUERY</TD><TD>#Counted.Total#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
